opening.argument: The video is presented as a coronavirus Q&A with a speaker who identifies himself as a professor of medicine and infectious diseases. His answers give practical health information: he discusses cleaners and sanitizers, recommends hand sanitizer after possible exposure, and emphasizes social distancing, isolation, and quarantining. The title frames the exchange as answers to questions from Twitter, consistent with the visible interview format. These are public-health explanations and precautions, not a transactional pitch or a promise of benefits. The interview and question format show no transactional or benefit-promise flow; the record supports an educational presentation without establishing any viewer purchase or promised outcome.

citations.quote: Dr. Martin Blaser Answers Coronavirus Questions From Twitter
I'm a professor of medicine and infectious diseases at Rutgers.
This coronavirus is very susceptible to soaps and sanitizers if they're used.
So after you have these exposures in a grocery store or elsewhere, you should use a hand. Sanitizer.
Social distancing, isolation, quarantining, these are all very important.
